clue.text: Comes together to look at wayside flowers maybe?

parts.note: to con is an old word for to study or examine closely
verges are roadside grass strips, where wild flowers grow

explanation.surface: Someone invites a friend to meet up and admire the flowers along a country lane.
explanation.walkthrough: VERGE is the British word for the grassy strip at the side of a road.
explanation.definitionFit: To converge is to move towards one point and meet, a direct synonym of coming together.

clue.text: City abroad that's ace on my birthday!

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the card letter is sent to the end

parts.note: cor! is a British exclamation of surprise, like my!
DOB is the abbreviation for date of birth
A is the card abbreviation for ace

explanation.surface: A traveller exclaims that a foreign city is wonderful on their birthday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'my!' is an exclamation, not a possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: Cordoba is a city in Spain and also in Argentina, so it is abroad for a British solver.

clue.text: Cars, say, interrupting the middle of siesta

indicators.note: one word breaking into another shows the synonym sits inside the letters taken from siesta
the central pair of letters of siesta are taken

parts.note: to state something is to say it

explanation.surface: A row of parked cars blocks someone's afternoon nap.
explanation.walkthrough: Estate car is the British term for a station wagon, which makes 'Cars' the definition rather than 'say'.
explanation.definitionFit: Estate cars are the British name for station wagons, so cars of that type are estates.

clue.text: Plants left in ancient marketplaces

indicators.note: the abbreviation is placed inside the plural word for marketplaces

parts.note: fora is the Latin plural of forum, a Roman marketplace

explanation.surface: Greenery abandoned among the ruins of Roman markets.
explanation.definitionFit: Flora is the collective term for the plant life of a region.

clue.text: Feature of cookery books one's penned as award-winner?

indicators.note: enclosed as in a pen, so the numeral is shut inside the other letters

parts.note: a recipe is a staple feature of cooking
I is the Roman numeral one; the 's is read as is
NT, the New Testament, is a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Someone wins a prize for writing the recipes in a cookbook.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'cookery books' as one phrase, but 'books' is NT; I sits inside RECIPENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who wins an award is its recipient, the person who receives it.

clue.text: Two similar medical departments finally negotiate agreement

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department of a hospital, taken twice
ENT is the ear, nose and throat department of a hospital, taken twice

indicators.note: only the closing letter of negotiate is used

explanation.surface: Two hospital departments reach a settlement after negotiation.
explanation.definitionFit: An entente is a friendly understanding between parties, as in the Entente Cordiale.

clue.text: Each European not half raring to go?

indicators.note: the second half of the nationality word is dropped, leaving its first three letters

parts.note: a German is a European

explanation.surface: Each European is only half keen to get going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not half' could read as British slang for 'very much', but here it trims GERMAN to GER.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone raring to go is keen and impatient to start, which is eager.

clue.text: Bishop participating in dance as one out of step

indicators.note: taking part in places the bishop inside the dance word

parts.note: a reel is a lively Scottish dance
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A bishop joins a dance but can't keep in step.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebel refuses to conform, figuratively out of step with everyone else.

clue.text: Became computerised, you understand?

parts.note: got means became, as in got angry
IT, information technology, describes computer systems

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether an office has finally gone digital.
explanation.definitionFit: Asking 'got it?' checks that the listener has understood.

clue.text: The whirlwind sweeping away the male bear

indicators.note: removing the pronoun from the phrase, as a whirlwind sweeps things off

parts.note: taken as written
an eddy is a swirling current of air or water
he is the male pronoun

explanation.surface: A whirlwind carries off a male bear.
explanation.walkthrough: THE EDDY loses HE, leaving TEDDY.
explanation.definitionFit: A teddy is a stuffed toy bear, named after US president Theodore Roosevelt, so the word is a synonym by name.

clue.text: Gift that is preceded by hug

indicators.note: the second piece comes after the first, so hug goes in front

parts.note: to press someone is to hug them close
IE is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A present handed over just after an embrace.
explanation.definitionFit: A pressie is an informal British word for a present or gift.

clue.text: Top teacher engaging boy in Religious Education will get listened to

indicators.note: taking on or holding, so the head contains the rest

parts.note: the head is the top teacher at a school

indicators.note: the boy's name is placed inside the subject abbreviation

parts.note: RE is the school abbreviation for Religious Education
Ken is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A head teacher takes on a boy in RE class and gets a hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: To hearken is an old word for to listen, so hearkened means listened to.

clue.text: Magic source of help supposedly when maiden goes off course

indicators.note: departs, so the letter for maiden leaves the word

parts.note: a mascot is supposed to bring good luck
M is the cricket abbreviation for maiden over

explanation.surface: A lucky charm loses its magic when a girl strays from the path.
explanation.walkthrough: ASCOT is a famous English racecourse.
explanation.definitionFit: Ascot is a racecourse in Berkshire, so it is a course.

clue.text: A wicked inclination can overwhelm a king — this was Midas's

indicators.note: surrounding and swamping, so the vice word encloses the rest

parts.note: a vice is a wicked habit or tendency
R is the abbreviation of rex, king

explanation.surface: A warning that a king can be overcome by greed, as Midas was.
explanation.walkthrough: King Midas of Greek myth was so greedy that he wished everything he touched to turn to gold.
explanation.definitionFit: Midas is the classic emblem of greed, so his failing was avarice.

clue.text: Teams catch a couple of them in an impossible situation!

definitions.meaning: cricket and football sides have eleven players

definitions.text: catch a couple of them in an impossible situation!
definitions.meaning: two of the number make twenty-two, as in the no-win trap Catch-22

explanation.definitionFit: Football and cricket teams of eleven players are known as elevens, and Catch-22 is two of them.

clue.text: One looking for company, perhaps, to be more green

parts.note: extra means additional, more
vert is the heraldic word for green

explanation.surface: A sociable person wants to become even more environmentally green.
explanation.definitionFit: An extravert is an outgoing person who seeks the company of others.

clue.text: Before Friday's end child always becomes happy

indicators.note: the pieces that follow come ahead of the last one

parts.note: e'er is a poetic contraction of ever, meaning always

indicators.note: only the final letter of Friday is used

explanation.surface: A child is always cheerful as the week ends on a Friday.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheery is a straightforward synonym of happy and bright.

clue.text: Incapable, having injected dangerous drug, that's obvious

indicators.note: the drug is put inside the other word, as in a syringe

parts.note: not able means incapable
ice is slang for crystal methamphetamine

explanation.surface: A person is plainly incapacitated after taking a dangerous drug.
explanation.definitionFit: Something noticeable is easy to see, so it is obvious.

clue.text: Legal rule established by good person among unruly people

indicators.note: placed amid, so the saint sits inside the rearranged letters
disorderly, so the letters of people are scrambled

parts.note: ST, saint, is a good person

explanation.surface: A rule of law laid down by a saint living among disorderly folk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unruly' gives EOPPEL from the letters of the people word; the saint sits after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Estoppel is a legal principle barring someone from denying what they earlier asserted.

clue.text: Romantic story of strangest expedition

indicators.note: the run of letters is taken from within the following words

explanation.surface: A romance about a very odd journey.
explanation.walkthrough: The run straddles strangEST Expedition. Beau Geste is the famous romantic adventure novel.
explanation.definitionFit: A geste is a tale of heroic deeds, a medieval romantic adventure story.

clue.text: Act peculiarly in desert, terribly distracted

indicators.note: the first scrambled piece is placed inside the second
badly, so the letters of desert are rearranged
oddly, so the letters of act are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone behaves strangely in the desert, badly unsettled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'peculiarly' gives CAT and 'terribly' gives STERED; the surface's single phrase 'desert, terribly distracted' hides two separate anagrams.
explanation.definitionFit: A scattered mind is distracted and unable to concentrate.

clue.text: Publicist deserving financial success

parts.note: PRO is a public relations officer, a publicist
fit means worthy or deserving

explanation.surface: A publicist earns the money they make.
explanation.definitionFit: Profit is the gain made in business, its financial success.

clue.text: One who travelled a long way for a game

definitions.text: One who travelled a long way
definitions.meaning: Marco, the Venetian merchant who journeyed to China
a sport played on horseback with mallets

explanation.definitionFit: Marco Polo was the famous medieval traveller, and polo is also a horseback ball game.

clue.text: Bird — a thing in the garden to be caught by cat?

indicators.note: captured inside, so the garden tool phrase goes inside the cat word

parts.note: a cat is a typical pet
a rake is a garden tool

explanation.surface: A bird in the garden at risk of being caught by the cat.
explanation.definitionFit: A parakeet is a small long-tailed parrot.

clue.text: I want to dine, spending time travelling all over the UK maybe

indicators.note: moving about, so the letters are rearranged once one has gone

explanation.surface: A diner keen to eat out tours the whole country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spending' drops a T from I WANT TO DINE; 'travelling' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Nationwide means across the whole nation, the UK being one example.

clue.text: Estate building so huge designed to accommodate goddess

indicators.note: to house, so the scrambled letters enclose the goddess
made to a new plan, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: Ate is the Greek goddess of mischief and ruin

explanation.surface: A huge building on an estate planned to house a goddess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'designed' turns SO HUGE into GHOUSE, with ATE inside after the G.
explanation.definitionFit: A gatehouse is the lodge at the entrance of a country estate.

clue.text: Grass enriched with organic material, not as a one-off operation

indicators.note: filled out with, so the material goes inside the grass word

parts.note: a reed is a tall waterside grass
peat is decomposed plant matter

explanation.surface: A lawn improved with compost, done more than once.
explanation.definitionFit: Something repeated happens again and again, rather than just once.

clue.text: James said eastern ruler should introduce a sporting event

indicators.note: spoken out loud, so the name is replaced by a word of the same sound

parts.note: Jim is the short form of James
a khan is a ruler in Central Asia

explanation.surface: A man named James declares that an Asian ruler should open a sporting contest.
explanation.definitionFit: A gymkhana is an equestrian event of horse races and games.

clue.text: After some tennis you won't want hard chair

indicators.note: the first piece comes before the rest

parts.note: a set is a portion of a tennis match

indicators.note: will do without, so the letter for hard is dropped

parts.note: thee is an old form of you
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: After tennis, a player would rather not sit on an uncomfortable seat.
explanation.walkthrough: THEE loses H to give TEE.
explanation.definitionFit: A settee is a long upholstered seat, a sofa, so a kind of chair.

clue.text: Learner that is lying around least likely to study?

indicators.note: spread about, so the Latin phrase encloses the learner letter

parts.note: id est is Latin for that is
L is the learner-driver plate letter

explanation.surface: A lazy student lies about doing nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: The idlest person is the laziest, and so least likely to study.

clue.text: Notice fitting offered by tailor

parts.note: an ad is a notice or advertisement
apt means suitable or fitting

explanation.surface: An advertisement for a suit fitting offered by a tailor.
explanation.definitionFit: To tailor something is to adjust or adapt it to a need.

clue.text: Signals made with rods

definitions.meaning: prompts telling someone when to act
the sticks used in snooker and billiards

explanation.definitionFit: Cues are both prompts to act and the sticks used in snooker.
